artists.biography:
The Carolina Chocolate Drops is an old-time string band from Durham, North Carolina, United States. Its 2010 album, Genuine Negro Jig, won the Grammy Award for Best Traditional Folk Album at the 53rd Annual Grammy Awards, and was number 9 in FRoots magazine's top 10 albums of 2010.
The Drops are one of the two known full-time African American string bands.

perplexity.description:
Genuine Negro Jig, the 2010 Grammy Award-winning album by Carolina Chocolate Drops, revitalizes the southern Black string band tradition through a masterful blend of blues, folk, world, and country influences. Formed by Dom Flemons, Rhiannon Giddens, and Justin Robinson after meeting at the 2005 Black Banjo Gathering in North Carolina, the trio trained under fiddler Joe Thompson, one of the last carriers of Piedmont banjo and fiddle styles. Produced by Joe Henry, the original record features silky smooth vocals, intricate instrumentation on banjo, fiddle, jug, kazoo, spoons, and bones, and tracks like "Hit 'Em Up Style," "Kissin' and Cussin'," and "Snowden's Jig (Genuine Negro Jig)" that fuse traditional arrangements with modern flair, evoking dusty, lamp-lit rooms alive with foot-stomping energy.

Critically acclaimed for its heart, soul, and historical depth, the album showcases the band's diverse backgrounds and shared singing duties, earning praise as an "artistically historic masterpiece" that bridges past and present American roots music. Reviewers hailed its unparalleled vocal proficiency and atmospheric power, with Giddens shining on bold covers and Robinson delivering tender traditional tunes like "Sandy Boys."

The 15th Anniversary Edition, released by Nonesuch Records in 2026, expands the original with nine bonus tracks—including seven previously unreleased recordings, a 2025 remaster of "City of Refuge," and a new mix of "Memphis Shakedown"—marking the album's first vinyl pressing since 2010. Highlights like "Here Rattler," learned from Grandpa Jones and John Snipes, feature Robinson on banjo, Giddens on fiddle, and Flemons on bones. Liner notes from Smithsonian experts affirm its enduring freshness and cultural impact, celebrated amid the band's 2025 reunion show.
